free_tier.stated: No free tier. XSIG-SE-0 is EUR 1.69 a month: 1 shared vCPU, 512 MiB RAM, 6 GiB SSD, 1 TiB traffic, a routed /64 IPv6 prefix and no IPv4 unless the EUR 0.65 a month add-on is bought.

retention.stated: the plan is billed per period and the disk persists while it is paid; no deletion grace period is printed on the page read

egress.terms: 1 TiB included on XSIG-SE-0, counted as the sum of inbound and outbound traffic

interface_detail: KVM guest with full root access and custom ISO support; a routed /64 (and a free /56 on request) means every port on any address in the prefix is reachable with no NAT layer and no port mapping.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; the vendor's own store runs on skhron.com.ua, which is behind a bot challenge to a non-browser client
chaining: the cleanest cheap WireGuard or monitor node: a routed /64 means the guest holds real addresses rather than a forwarded port, and NAT64 gives outbound reach to IPv4-only destinations

limits.value: 1 TiB a month, inbound and outbound summed, on the cheapest rung
0.06 vCPU guaranteed on the 1-core rung, bursting to 1 vCPU under the fair-use policy

binding_note: 1 TiB a month counted in both directions is the first thing a WireGuard node or a busy monitor will exhaust; the CPU guarantee is second.

identity_cost.detail: the vendor states 'No KYC is required to order or use our services'. Payment rails are Bitcoin, Bitcoin Lightning, Monero, Tron, Bitcoin Cash and other crypto through a self-hosted processor, plus Visa, Mastercard and SEPA. No card hold is stated on any page read. The checkout form itself was not reached: the store host skhron.com.ua returns a Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode challenge (HTTP 402) to a non-browser client.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the vendor publishes a 99.95% uptime claim and states services that draw sustained attacks may be filtered or null-routed
confidence_note: price, shape, traffic term, the routed /64 statement, the NAT64 statement and the EUR 0.65 IPv4 add-on are quoted from the vendor's own Sweden page read. The order URL is the one the page's own Order button targets but it was not followed to a rendered checkout because the store host challenges non-browser clients, so the cart is unverified while the price is documented.

evidence.proved: quoted plan card: 'XSIG-SE-0 ... CPU Cores 1 (shared) 0.06 vCPU is guaranteed, bursts up to 1 vCPU according to FUP ... Memory 512 MiB ... Disk space 6 GiB SSD ... Traffic incl. 1 TiB ... Price € 1.69'
quoted: 'Every VPS includes a routed /64 IPv6 prefix at no extra cost. A routed /56 prefix is available free of charge upon request.'
quoted: 'IPv4 address is not included, but it is available as an add-on at €0.65 per month per address. Each IPv4 address you add is dedicated to your server.'
quoted: 'Yes. Your server can reach IPv4-only services like GitHub through our NAT64 gateway.' and 'IPv4-only networks can't reach your server without a dedicated IPv4 address.'

quoted: 'No KYC is required to order or use our services.' and 'Founded in Ukraine and registered in Estonia, Skhron has served hundreds of customers since 2023'; payment rails listed as Bitcoin, Bitcoin Lightning, Monero, Tron, Bitcoin Cash, 'Traditional payments via Visa, Mastercard, and SEPA'

the Order button's target, read from the page source. Following it returned 'Bot Fight Mode: skhron.com.ua' at HTTP 402 with an 8-word body, so the checkout was not read; skhron.eu/store/... returns 404, so the .com.ua host is the live store

notes: The best IPv6-only row in the band on the two properties that matter: a routed /64 rather than a single address, and a NAT64 gateway so the guest can still reach IPv4-only destinations outbound. EUR 1.69 a month is EUR 20.28 a year if billed monthly; the vendor also advertises an annual discount but the annual figure was not read on this page. The EUR 0.65 a month IPv4 add-on is the cheapest conversion to a reachable dual-stack box found: EUR 2.34 a month total, which is still under the line. Not established: the checkout form's fields, whether the card rail takes a debit or prepaid card, any card hold, the renewal price, and stock. The store host being a different TLD from the marketing site is worth knowing before buying, and its bot challenge means a buyer should expect to complete the order in a real browser.
